paper.title_en: Performance study of a customized silicon photodiode for the dual-readout HERD calorimeter
paper.abstract_en: The High Energy cosmic-Radiation Detection (HERD) facility, proposed by the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is a space astronomy and particle astrophysics payload set for deployment onboard the China Space Station in 2029. The core of HERD is a 3D imaging calorimeter with two independent readout systems: one employing wavelength-shifting fibers coupled to intensified CMOS cameras, and the other adopting silicon photo-diodes (PD) coupled to a dedicated ASIC. Complementary to one another, the two readout systems support mutual cross-validation, thereby improving the overall reliability of the detector. The PD readout system coupled to LYSO crystals is required to achieve a large dynamic range of 10$^{7}$, covering deposited energies from 30 MeV to 300 TeV. To match the relatively small dynamic range of the ASIC (about 10$^{3}$), a customized three-in-one PD module has been designed and developed, integrating a large-area PD (LPD, 6 × 6 mm$^{2}$), a medium-area PD (MPD, 1.2 × 1.2 mm$^{2}$ with a 20% transmittance filter), and a small-area PD (SPD, 1.2 × 1.2 mm$^{2}$ with a 0.2% transmittance filter). For the beam test prototype, more than 600 such three-PD modules were produced in a small-scale batch. A dedicated batch testing system with 8-channel switching capability was developed to characterise the dark current and junction capacitance of the PD modules. In addition, sampling tests were carried out on the photosensitivity, rise time, and energy linearity. The measured performance of the first batch of customized three-in-one PD modules demonstrates that all key parameters meet or surpass the design targets, thereby underpinning the feasibility of the PD readout scheme for the HERD calorimeter.
